title: CSPG4 tissue RNA in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma: an exploratory comparison across sarcoma cohorts
abstract:
Background: The interpretation of CSPG4 RNA in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) depends on the sarcoma used for comparison. We examined whether the observed differences recur across datasets.

Methods: We compared a fixed panel of 11 genes in nine EMC tumors and 45 tumors from three other sarcoma types. A second dataset contained six EMC biopsies and 17 low-grade fibromyxoid sarcomas (LGFMS). We retained the original panel rule, individual comparator results and sensitivity analyses. CHRNA6 was a separate RNA-marker control.

Results: CSPG4 RNA was higher in EMC than in LGFMS in both datasets: the probability-of-superiority score A was 1.000 in the arrays and 0.966 in the RNA-sequencing cohort, where 0.5 indicates neutral ordering. Other specified comparisons were also positive, but the comparison with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans was not (A=0.467). CSPG4 alone met the original panel rule. Its primary composite was 0.895 using all years and 0.811 within sequencing years. Only four EMC patients supported the matched composite. Removing the 2019 group left two matchable EMC patients and reversed that composite to 0.433; the all-year composite remained positive at 0.833.

Conclusions: These small public cohorts support a recurring CSPG4 RNA difference against LGFMS, alongside comparator dependence and sparse matching support. They provide descriptive evidence for studies of EMC tissue, without establishing diagnostic accuracy, malignant-cell protein localization or therapeutic suitability.
